Reports mapping coverage explicitly: how many of the tested zebrafish genes (and how many of the significant genes) received a 1:1 human ortholog call versus many:many or no call

Does not silently drop or collapse many:many ortholog relationships without flagging them in the output

steps.name: Human pathway enrichment via ortholog-mapped genes
caveats: This step depends entirely on ortholog-mapping quality from T2S2 — report enrichment results alongside the ortholog coverage rate so readers can judge how representative the mapped gene set is of the full DE signal
Do not conflate 'enriched in the human-ortholog-mapped set' with 'the zebrafish pathway is active' — state this distinction directly in reported output
steps.question: Which human-curated pathways (WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark, GO, and canonical KEGG-MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) are enriched among the human orthologs of the zebrafish genes differentially expressed between treated and control larvae?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the 1:1-ortholog-mapped significant gene list from T2S2 as foreground and the full mapped tested-gene list as background/universe

Tests against WikiPathways human, MSigDB Hallmark human, MSigDB GO (BP/CC/MF) human, and MSigDB canonical pathways human (KEGG-MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) gene sets, each reported separately with BH-adjusted p-values
If any of these reference GMTs are not resolvable in the environment at run time, the step reports which ones ran and which were skipped rather than failing silently

Every enrichment hit is reported with the caveat that it reflects the human ortholog's annotated pathway membership, not a zebrafish-validated pathway — findings are translational/inferential, not zebrafish-native evidence

steps.name: Synthesis of DE genes and enriched pathways
caveats: Do not overstate confidence in pathway calls given the small sample size and the reliance on ortholog mapping for the human-resource half of the enrichment
steps.question: Summarizing across the native zebrafish GO enrichment and the ortholog-based human pathway enrichment, which genes differ between treated and control zebrafish larvae and which pathways do they point to?
acceptance_criteria: Combines the DESeq2 significant gene list (T1S1), native GO enrichment (T2S1), and human ortholog pathway enrichment (T2S3) into one consolidated table/report

Clearly separates findings that are zebrafish-native (GO via org.Dr.eg.db) from findings that required cross-species ortholog inference (WikiPathways/MSigDB human), stating the ortholog coverage rate from T2S2 alongside any human-pathway claim
States explicitly that this is a single-batch, n=3-per-group study, so pathway-level conclusions should be read as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory

plan.title: Zebrafish larvae DE + pathway enrichment, drug vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a small bulk RNA-seq experiment (12000 genes x 6 samples, salmon gene-level counts on Ensembl Danio rerio annotation) with a clean two-group unpaired design (3 treated vs 3 control zebrafish larvae pools, single batch). This supports a standard DESeq2 negative-binomial differential expression workflow without batch correction. No zebrafish-specific pathway gene-set reference (WikiPathways zebrafish, zebrafish MSigDB) is staged in this environment — only human and mouse GMTs and org.Dr.eg.db (present) are available for zebrafish. The plan therefore: (1) runs QC + DESeq2 DE directly on the zebrafish counts using org.Dr.eg.db for ID/annotation bookkeeping; (2) maps the resulting zebrafish DE gene list to human orthologs using babelgene (installed, offline, supports Danio rerio -> Homo sapiens ortholog tables) so that the rich human pathway resources (WikiPathways human, MSigDB hallmark/GO/canonical human) can be used for enrichment, since no native zebrafish GMT is staged; (3) also runs GO enrichment natively in zebrafish space via clusterProfiler/org.Dr.eg.db (GO terms are organism-native and don't require ortholog mapping), giving a native-species check alongside the ortholog-based human-pathway enrichment. Both enrichment routes are reported side by side, and the ortholog-mapping step's incomplete coverage is flagged explicitly rather than treated as a complete 1:1 mapping.
